findings.body:
chunk 1/2:

Command strings return before `detectPotentialUnredactedSecret` runs. A command containing an opaque credential in an `X-Auth` header therefore retains it in the durable snapshot, even though the same token is hidden by the full-view sanitizer. The raw-input path is verified at `inline-agent-loop-tools.ts:351`, and `durable-interaction-handler.ts:181` persists this projection. There is also a partial-redaction case: `KEY_VALUE_PATTERN` in `sensitive-material.ts:151` treats an escaped double quote as the end of a password value, so a valid assignment such as `PGPASSWORD="prefix\"suffix"` leaves the credential suffix stored and visible in full views. These command cases are new evidence beyond the repaired field-name and shortening cases. Mask complete credential spans and apply the opaque-secret fallback before storing commands; cover both cases in the existing secret regression table.
findings.title: Not done: command credentials are hidden in durable snapshots

findings.body:
chunk 1/2:

The formatter recognizes conversation markup anywhere in the text, including an already-extracted user request. For example, a request saying `Count <messages> elements in this XML file` is extracted and unescaped successfully, but the snapshot calls `permissionRequestWhyText` again. This check then classifies that plain request as a formatted conversation, finds no `<message>` wrapper, and returns undefined at line 191. Consequently, every provider loses its Why line. Recognize the actual conversation envelope once and preserve literal tags in extracted request text.
findings.title: Preserve literal XML tags in the request-derived why line

stop.reason: Owner: keep it simple, like Claude Code.
